title: Garden and Hollow
premise: Juniper Pemberton keeps the ledgers of the Hollow Guild, which trades in impossible things, while hiding her forbidden gift of beast-speech. When a century-old prophecy book names tonight's date as the night the Long Winter begins, she discovers the prophecy's villain is King Aldous—already hollowed and replaced by the crown itself, a parasite of cold that eats memory. Guided by a prophecy-ghost named Sorrel and the wolf she secretly loves, Juniper must unbind the true king from his crown by trading her own most precious memory. In the end she saves the kingdom, but wakes with no memory of the wolf or her love—until the beasts remember for her, and the story closes with her relearning her own heart.
about_author: Wren Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild ledgers and now writes fantasies about the people who keep the books. They live in a drafty house with a talkative cat and a stubborn belief that every prophecy is a filing error waiting to be corrected.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She audits the Hollow Guild's strangest entries—a bottled echo, a debt paid in years—while hiding her gift from her supervisor. Emotional beat: quiet dread of discovery, and pride in her careful, invisible life.

chapters.title: A Date in an Old Book
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Cataloguing a confiscated prophecy, she finds tonight's exact date circled a century ago, with her guild's sigil beside it. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of an ordinary evening.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Said
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the guild roof she speaks with the city wolves, who warn that winter is coming early and wrong. Emotional beat: the gift is a burden, but the wolves are her only truth-tellers.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Summons
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Hesse's POV. He knows Juniper's secret and assigns her to the prophecy investigation, both trusting and using her. Emotional beat: being seen is not the same as being safe.

chapters.title: Sorrel, Who Waited a Century
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the prophecy's margin she meets Sorrel, a ghost anchored to the book, who claims to have written it. Emotional beat: eerie wonder and an instant, prickly alliance.

chapters.title: The King Who Smiled Wrong
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, attending a royal audit. King Aldous is courteous, cold, and does not blink enough. Emotional beat: horror dressed in courtly manners.

chapters.title: The Crown That Eats
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV, a flashback chapter. A hundred years ago, Sorrel watched a young king accept a crown forged to hold winter at bay—and the crown began to hold him instead. Emotional beat: tragic inevitability.

chapters.title: Beast-Speech Is Treason
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A guild informer glimpses her speaking to a horse; she buys his silence with a ledger favor she'll regret. Emotional beat: the first compromise that will cost her.

chapters.title: The Wolf at the Winter Gate
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She meets Ash, a wolf who can take human shape, sent by the northern packs to investigate the early frost. Emotional beat: recognition—two hidden things finding each other.

chapters.title: Ledgers Do Not Lie, People Do
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She finds entries altered to hide shipments of 'cold' to the palace. Hesse warns her off. Emotional beat: the guild she trusted is complicit.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Missing Page
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. He and Juniper learn the prophecy's final page was torn out and sold through the guild decades ago. Emotional beat: frustration sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Market of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She infiltrates the guild's black auction to find the page, trading a memory of her mother's voice as payment. Emotional beat: grief as currency; the cost of the quest made literal.

chapters.title: The Page That Names Her
chapters.summary: Juniper and Ash's alternating POV. The recovered page names a 'ledger-keeper with the beasts' tongue' as the unbinding. Emotional beat: chosen by prophecy is not the same as chosen by anyone who loves you.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wants
chapters.summary: King Aldous's POV, brief and fractured. The crown's hunger surfaces; the true king screams beneath. Emotional beat: pity for the monster, terror of it.

chapters.title: First Snow in Harvest Month
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Snow falls out of season; the city panics; the guild profits. Emotional beat: anger at systems that monetize catastrophe.

chapters.title: Ash's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. The packs demand he abandon the human and report; he refuses and is exiled. Emotional beat: love chosen over belonging.

chapters.title: Hesse Confesses
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Hesse admits the guild has fed the crown 'cold' for a century to keep trade flowing through the Long Winter. Emotional beat: betrayal by the father-figure.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Regret
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. The ghost admits she forged the prophecy's ending to give future generations a weapon—Juniper—and asks forgiveness. Emotional beat: the weight of being someone's plan.

chapters.title: The Palace Library
chapters.summary: Juniper and Ash's POV. They infiltrate the palace and find the crown's origin: it was made from a frozen god's fingerbone. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The King in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper reaches the true Aldous, imprisoned behind his own smiling face; he begs her not to save him if it costs the kingdom. Emotional beat: compassion for a stranger who asks to be let die.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Guildhall
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The informer she bribed sells her out; Hesse hands her to the crown's wardens. Emotional beat: the trap of every compromise coming due at once.

chapters.title: The Cold Room
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, imprisoned. The crown offers her a deal: her memories for the kingdom's warmth. Emotional beat: despair, then a hard, clear-eyed 'no.'

chapters.title: The Packs Come South
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash breaks exile, leading the wolf packs against the palace wardens. Emotional beat: fury and devotion in equal measure.

chapters.title: Sorrel Burns the Book
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. To free Juniper, Sorrel sacrifices her anchor—burning the prophecy and her own existence. Emotional beat: a ghost choosing an ending; grief and gratitude.

chapters.title: Escape Across the Ice
chapters.summary: Juniper and Ash's POV. Fleeing the burning palace quarter, they shelter in the frozen gardens and finally speak their love aloud. Emotional beat: tenderness at the edge of doom.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Sorrel's last message reveals the rite: the unbinding requires a memory of equal weight to a king's whole reign. Emotional beat: understanding the true price.

chapters.title: What Juniper Chooses to Forget
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She secretly prepares the trade: not her mother's voice, but her memories of Ash. Emotional beat: quiet, devastating resolve; she tells no one.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Multiple POV, interludes. The crown stops pretending; winter swallows the city in hours. Emotional beat: apocalyptic urgency.

chapters.title: Storming the Throne
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. The wolves and Juniper fight to the throne room through the crown's frozen warden-guard. Emotional beat: courage as a choice made again with every step.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Confrontation with the crown-entity, which offers her a kingdom of her own in exchange for walking away. Emotional beat: temptation met with contempt.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, climax. She performs the rite, pouring her love for Ash into the crown as the price; the entity unravels and the true Aldous dies free. Emotional beat: sacrifice at full cost, rendered in sensory detail.

chapters.title: Spring, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Winter breaks; the city thaws; Juniper wakes with a hole in her heart she cannot name. Emotional beat: hollow victory; grief without an object.

chapters.title: The Wolf Who Waits
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash keeps his distance, honoring her sacrifice, visiting only as a wolf at her window. Emotional beat: love that refuses to demand.

chapters.title: The Beasts Remember
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The city animals keep telling her about 'the wolf she loved,' and she begins keeping a new ledger of their testimony. Emotional beat: mourning becoming investigation.

chapters.title: Hesse's Ledger, Closed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She exposes the guild's century of complicity and rebuilds it as a house of restitution, taking the master's chair. Emotional beat: justice as slow, unglamorous work.

chapters.title: The New King's Debt
chapters.summary: Juniper and the regent's POV. The dead king's heir owes Juniper a crown-debt; she asks not for gold but for sanctuary for the packs. Emotional beat: power used gently.

chapters.title: What Ash Gave Up
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Juniper learns the packs exiled him for her, and that he has never once tried to win her memory back. Emotional beat: the ethics of loving someone who chose to forget you.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Us
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She reads the beasts' testimony aloud to herself nightly, courting her own lost love like a stranger. Emotional beat: hope as deliberate practice.

chapters.title: First Frost, Second Chance
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the anniversary, she asks Ash to tell her their whole story; the telling cracks the rite's seal, and one memory returns—his name. Emotional beat: a single word carrying the weight of everything.

chapters.title: Garden and Hollow
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, resolution. Memory returns like spring, not all at once; she and Ash plant the palace gardens where the crown's cold once lived, and she writes the last line of a new prophecy: 'the ledger-keeper kept.' Emotional beat: restoration earned, love remembered into being.
